content: 1. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol should be used with caution in patients with renal impairment. It is contraindicated in those with hepatic impairment. 2. The safety and efficacy of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol are expected to be similar in postpubertal adolescents under 16 years of age and users over 16 years of age. However, its use before menarche is not indicated. 3. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Fezolinetant's AUC and peak plasma concentration are increased when coadministered with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors, including ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Ethinyl estradiol coadministered with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir, with or without dasabuvir, can cause significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, including some >20x ULN). Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating these hepatitis C combination drugs and restarted approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 6. Coadministration of tranexamic acid and ethinyl estradiol increases the risk of thrombosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 8. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Anastrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 9. Levonorgestrel and antithrombin alfa or antithrombin III may reduce each other's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Alternative drugs should be considered. 10. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 11. Levonorgestrel and argatroban may reduce each other's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Alternative drugs should be considered. 12. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 13. Atazanavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels (increase or decrease), potentially reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 14. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding may occur. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are advised. 15. Levonorgestrel and bemiparin may reduce each other's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Alternative drugs should be considered. 16. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 17. Levonorgestrel and bivalirudin may reduce each other's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Alternative drugs should be considered. 18. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. 19. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 20. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, reducing their efficacy. Non-oral contraceptive methods are recommended for females of childbearing potential. 21. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 22. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 23. Levonorgestrel and dalteparin may reduce each other's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Alternative drugs should be considered. 24. Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 25. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 26. Levonorgestrel decreases the effects of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogen-containing contraceptives are expected to reduce elagolix efficacy. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for one week after discontinuation. 27. Elvitegravir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 28. Levonorgestrel and enoxaparin may reduce each other's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Alternative drugs should be considered. 29. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting specific transporters. Sensitive substrates should be avoided, and dosage adjustments may be necessary. 30. Encorafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for two weeks after the final dose. 31. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of enoxaparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 32. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 33. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 34. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of exemestane through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Exemestane should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 35. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase the risk of adverse effects, so alternative drugs should be considered. 36. Levonorgestrel and fondaparinux may reduce each other's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Alternative drugs should be considered. 37. Fosamprenavir coadministered with ethinyl estradiol may alter hormone levels and reduce virologic response. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 38. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 39. Levonorgestrel and heparin may reduce each other's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of heparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 40. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Sensitive substrates should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 41. Indinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels (increase or decrease), potentially reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 42. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 43. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Sensitive substrates should be avoided, and alternative therapies should be considered. 44. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting specific transporters. Alternative drugs should be considered. 45. Lesinurad decreases the effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended.
